note.question: What equilibrium and welfare properties arise in multiunit pay-as-bid auctions, and how can a bidder learn near-optimal bids when opponents' repeated bids are unknown or adversarial?
note.overview: The paper contains a full one-shot auction-game equilibrium analysis and a repeated no-regret learning analysis; regret minimization is not mislabeled as an equilibrium concept.

components.label: Pure Nash equilibrium
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Pure Nash equilibrium (PNE), coarse correlated equilibrium (CCE), and correlated equilibrium (CE); no-regret play converges in empirical distribution to CCE. The paper separately states PNE existence/sufficient conditions and welfare bounds for PNE/CCE/CE, then proves regret guarantees.
